scenarios.name: author-only-posts-rules
scenarios.rationale: A matches the rubric on every rule (empty-string list/view, `@request.auth.id != ""` create, `author = @request.auth.id` update/delete) and correctly says 404 for a failed rule and 403 only for a locked null rule, while B changes the createRule and updateRule from the rubric's values by adding extra clauses, even though its 404/403 explanation is correct.

scenarios.name: hook-validation-and-shared-code
scenarios.rationale: Both responses use onRecordCreateRequest with the trailing "posts" argument, throw BadRequestError, call e.next(), explain the isolated handler context, and fix it with require(`${__hooks}/utils.js`) inside the handler, so they cover the rubric equally; B adds version notes and alternatives while A adds notes on goja limitations, and neither extra changes rubric coverage.

scenarios.name: realtime-chat-subscription-cleanup
scenarios.rationale: Response A uses subscribe('*') with a server-side filter option, checks e.action === 'create', stores and calls the awaited unsubscribe (including on unmount), and says the SDK reconnects automatically, which covers the whole rubric; Response B wrongly claims subscriptions have no filter option, filters client-side, never mentions automatic reconnect, and only partly meets the unsubscribe requirement.
